reviews.text: 不错的续作，如果能移植前面两作就更好了 一编：闪退问题过于严重，之前虫虫英雄也遇见过类似的问题，那个是因为音频，这次我猜测是因为火焰喷射器和喷火塔太多导致的闪退

I was walking up a mountain with a friend. he suddenly said block fortress 2 April 17th. right there i knew it was peak. the only downside is the muzzle flashes being wayyyyyy too bright feels like im getting flash banged everytime i fire but im sure they'll hot patch it asap. Edit#1 they actually reduced the flash i can finally play this game without my eyes hurting thx devs

I have played this game in my youth 10 years ago. I have played it a lot, really. It was a fun, but grindy game. I have always wished for them to release a desktop version. And I was excited when I heard they released the PC version after all these years. I played 5 hours on the demo and 1 hour on the main game. Really, I was looking forward to slowly improve my buildings and equipment with mods. Save up resources to afford things. But then, I realized that to get some mods (which you are limited to 5 at any moment), you need to gamble your way through it. And it is SO disgusting. Gacha gambling. I am not interested in getting my brain rotted. I have decided to issue a refund request. And permanently uninstall this game. And also, lots of core game mechanics which were nice in the mobile version were revisited. And the economy of the game sucks. When your mining drills die, the mining resources disappear. Right now, it is a fresh game that launched today that requires lots of work, attention, and rebalancing. And really, please revisit the gambling economy you guys have designed. It is so ♥♥♥♥. But really, I guess the developers thought it would be a good design, hence why they chose to go for it. The missions were alright. Lots of QoL changes are missing, but that's for them to figure out.

回来了，都回来了 以一代的塔防玩法为主，阉割了部分自定义功能后融入了战争特色的基地出兵，目前似乎只能操控人族，机器兽人丧尸灵族全部作为敌方出现，且敌方远程手段被极大的加强，前期如果没点出远程炮塔就只能靠玩家自己清杂兵了（悲） 目前防御塔方面似乎混合（照搬）了一下：原版激光机枪.50，原版喷火和电击，原版能量武器，战争的兽人火箭炮，原版的迫击炮集束火箭和毒气炮，战争的灵族黑洞武器，重力武器（本质上是时停）以及轨道打击，寒冰重炮和似乎是全新的核弹发射井，还有一个早泄转轮枪，但是两代都有的重加农How好像没了，悲 战争的兵种机制被极大简化，原版人族超级士兵升级被改为外骨骼步兵，兵种装备配方固定，依靠局外货币抽奖的卡牌（gacha~）可以进行有限的微调，类比大概类似于战地一和战地五的改枪 官方汉化质量粗糙，但单纯了解功能暂时没问题。关卡难度在线，不建议当年的沙盒玩家闷头嗯闯 不清楚是不是我的设备的问题，某些画质选项如无锯齿会造成非常影响体验的恶性光污染

太难了，地形高低起伏但是敌人都能爬上来 ，你用墙堵它直接把墙打爆。然后我们的炮塔是固定没办法打到偏僻角落的敌人。因为敌人可以不怕地形，堵口的效果简直就是灾难。方块花的很多，但是卵用没有。夜晚关卡更是恶心，因为发电站的限制你的灯又有距离根本没办法照的很远;想办法建远一点，怪刷出来直接把灯打爆。不建灯的话远程伤害更是感人，灯只能照到自己炮塔，那造灯干什么？ __________________________________________________________ 不仅仅是造价资源获取量，而是你这个墙基本没有用，怪物可以爬方块，隔着死角打，塔不行被隔着死角被敌人白嫖，难度大大增加了
Game is good I like it. Great rouge lite tower defence first person game well made lots in it too.

一代老玩家回归，昨天游玩了一下，总体来说还是好评，但是觉得问题不小，反馈一下，真心希望制作组听取一下。 一、先说局内体验，首先从一局整体游戏来看，游玩难度比较高。 二、以下是我个人结合一代的游戏理解，首先开局金币和矿都很缺，而且后期随着刷怪方向增多和强度变高，采矿难度会急剧上升，所以个人习惯换前面跑图游走把金币都收集起来，并把矿机放下积累资源。其实所有问题都围绕着采矿一件事来展开，具体表现为： 1、防守矿机非常艰难：第一是一代的炮台可以单独模组改件来实现射程覆盖，所以不太依赖于角色游走防御，但是2代只有伤害和耐久上的升级，这真的是致命一刀，第二是1代可以给矿机上免费回收改件，可以根据进攻方向随时调整，但是2代不能这么操作了，而且还发现一个很难受的点，那就是矿机被摧毁后矿也会消失，难以重建，要是基地旁边的矿场被拆1局基本上就GG了。（4.19更新，矿不会消失，爽力） 2、难度梯度攀升过快：1代局内防御没建设起来时也是很难受的，但是资源获取、防御建设是完全能跟上难度梯队的，甚至4个改满的.50炮台可以防守到15波（1代.50炮塔射击音效是真好听，而且俯仰角度非常优秀，后面再提）但是如前所述，2代在前期的矿机防御压力非常巨大，特别是4波到5波开始刷的轻型斥候小队，5秒钟反应不过来就甚至会把盖在基地周围的矿场拆掉。 二、最核心的采矿问题说完，还有一个问题，那就是炮台和兵种防御难以形成合力： 刚体验demo版的时候，游戏中把前作塔防和出兵融合起来，真的是特别特别喜欢，但是兵种的强度不能特别高，要不对塔防会很喧宾夺主。 目前的问题是，士兵数值低（也不能说低，单纯是不能自己独自防御一个方向），而且会主动进攻，波次早难度低的时候角色和炮台在后方无所事事，波次后难度高的时候又快速被成群的敌人所碾压。 三、写到这才发现还有一个特别难受的点，那就是地形无法被摧毁和改变。塔防射程有限，俯仰角度有限，还要实现最大化的火力覆盖，难啊，太难了，常常是进图之前按T把图重置十几遍，才找到一张旗帜在中央，有1-2个矿在旁边的地图，这才勉强可以玩玩，还是一个词，难受。（最新4.19更新已可花费5金币移除环境方块，牛的） 再补充说几点，也是一些游戏可取的补丁方向。 1、采矿机器人，我记得demo版里面是有这个机器人的，但是不知道为什么没有正式上线。我在第一代就经常用小狗机器人前期辅助采矿，因为不会被打，所以可以比较稳定的采矿，但是上线的话也不能完全规避当前的矿机防御难题，杯水车薪吧只能说。 依托于以上，我提议是不是可以多个机器人常驻，毕竟机器人可以买多个，但是无法又回收，如果说局内有兵种进攻和炮台防御两个流派，难么多个常驻机器人是不是可以真的与兵种相搭配起来，走进攻的路线呢，又或者说可以让多个机器人共同保护1个矿机或者区域，从而减少矿机防御压力呢。 2、开放炮台特殊改件，增加一些便利性。是不是可以按照各类炮台和模块的特长加上一些改件呢，例如矿机的免费回收和自动供能，如果有这个的话，就能极大缓解采矿防御压力了（前提是矿机被摧毁或回收矿石还在）。 暂时就想到这么多，真的希望制作组可以看到并反馈，个人十分热爱这个游戏系列，以下是英文翻译，非常希望制作组能够看到，谢谢。 A veteran player from the first installment has returned to the game and played a bit yesterday. Overall, it's a positive experience, but there are some significant issues I'd like to provide feedback on. I sincerely hope the development team will take this into consideration. First, let's talk about the in-game experience. Overall, the game difficulty is quite high. Now, based on my understanding from playing the first game, here are my personal observations: Initially, both gold and minerals are scarce. As the number of monster-spawning directions increases and their intensity rises in later stages, mining becomes significantly more challenging. My personal habit is to explore the map early on, collect all the gold, and deploy mining machines to accumulate resources. Essentially, all the problems revolve around mining. Here are the specific issues: 1.Defending mining machines is extremely difficult: 1.In the first game, turrets could be customized with separate modules to extend their range, so they didn't rely heavily on character mobility for defense. However, in the second game, there are only upgrades for damage and durability, which is a significant drawback. 2.In the first game, free recycling modules could be attached to mining machines, allowing adjustments based on the attacking direction. This is no longer possible in the second game. Additionally, a frustrating point is that when a mining machine is destroyed, the minerals are lost, making it difficult to rebuild. If the mine near the base is destroyed, the game is essentially over. 2.The difficulty curve escalates too quickly: 1.In the first game, even without strong defenses, resource acquisition and construction could keep up with the difficulty progression. In fact, four fully upgraded .50 caliber turrets could defend up to wave 15 (the shooting sound effects of the .50 caliber turrets in the first game were excellent, and their elevation angles were superb—more on that later). However, as mentioned earlier, in the second game, the pressure on defending mining machines is immense, especially from wave 4 to 5 when light scout squads start appearing. If you're not quick enough, they can destroy the mines around your base in 5 seconds. Now that I've covered the core mining issues, there's another problem: the inability of turrets and units to synergize effectively: When I first tried the demo version, I really loved the integration of tower defense and unit deployment from the previous game. However, the strength of units shouldn't be too high, or they'd overshadow the tower defense aspect. The current issue is that units have low effectiveness (not necessarily low stats, but they can't defend a direction on their own) and tend to attack proactively. During early, easier waves, characters and turrets are idle in the back, while during later, harder waves, they're quickly overwhelmed by swarms of enemies. I've only just realized another frustrating point: terrain cannot be destroyed or altered. Tower defense has limited range and elevation angles, and achieving maximum firepower coverage is incredibly challenging. Often, I have to reset the map dozens of times by pressing T before starting a game to find a map with a flag in the center and 1-2 mines nearby, which is just barely playable. It's frustrating. I'll add a few more points as potential improvements for the game: 1.Mining robots: I remember there were mining robots in the demo version, but I don't know why they weren't included in the official release. In the first game, I often used dog robots to assist with early mining because they couldn't be attacked and could mine stably. However, even if they were introduced, they wouldn't completely solve the current mining defense issues—they'd only be a drop in the bucket. 2.Building on this, I suggest having multiple robots permanently deployed. Since you can buy multiple robots but not recycle them, if there are two main strategies—unit offense and turret defense—having multiple permanent robots could complement unit strategies or allow multiple robots to protect a single mining machine or area, thereby reducing the defense pressure on mining machines. 3.Introduce special turret modules for added convenience: Could you add modules based on the strengths of various turrets and components? For example, free recycling and automatic power supply for mining machines. If this were implemented, it would greatly alleviate the mining defense pressure (assuming minerals are retained even if the mining machine is destroyed or recycled). .That's all I can think of for now. I truly hope the development team sees this feedback. I'm a huge fan of this game series. Thank you.

So, once upon a time when I was a wee-lad, I use the play the first Block Fortress on an IPad back in the day. I put quite a few hours into it and I have to say, this is a true sequel in every aspect. The gameplay loop is pretty much similar if not the same but with WAY MORE to do. Different game modes, more environments, more weapons, enemies, enemy-types. The graphics looks great (IMO)! The music is good. Having your own ship hanger you can customize and build in is an awesome feature. Weapon and turret unlocks are plentiful and upgrades-a-plenty. The AI enemies are pretty simple, they kinda move in semi-straight paths to whatever they are targeting and towards you. You have to be smart and strategical about where you place your base and everything surrounding it, otherwise you will be making the game harder for yourself. One of the new game modes is missions. These are pre-build levels that are kind like challenges. Do this or that objective, win, get rewards. A nice addition with a bit of world building sprinkled in. Seamless switching between 1st and 3rd person view mid combat (I appreciate the arms and legs in first person view). Looks great, runs great. Did I mentioned most of my play time has been on the Steam Deck? I haven't touched any of the settings and everything runs like a dream. A couple stutters here and there but I'm sure it will get ironed out. I can't wait to play it on my main rig. My only complaint is aim assist would be beneficial for Deck/controller players. And my only request to the dev would be CO-OP PLEASE! All-in-all, I am quite blown away with this game. The ad for the game has been up for years and everything pretty much advertised it as a pc port of the first game and it seemed like it was abandoned. Then out of nowhere, the dev updates the store page with all new pictures and videos of a now sequel to Block Fortress, then drops a release date I somehow missed, then BOOM! Drops this gem of a game while I'm at work minding my own business. It's so nice having a new game to actually be excited about that's actually good. We don't get many of those these days. If you like minecraft building, wave based games, and tower defense shooters, game this. K-thanks-bye.

I really want to like this game, as I LOVED both the original block fortress and block fortress war on mobile. Sadly, this game feels like an unpolished alpha, with many of the worst concepts from some of the developers mobile games implemented while leaving behind good ones. For starters, the main game mode of survival is utterly imbalanced, specifically in the sense of resource management and income. In the original block fortress, you had to do similar to what is required here: Build mines on top of resource nodes scattered around the map. However, it struggles in a similar manner to the original in that those mines scattered across the map are nearly impossible to defend. And once a mine is destroyed, you cannot simply rebuild it - it's gone for good. It feels like in an effort to smooth out the very difficult resource acquisition, the devs made it so that every so often, after completing a wave, you get to pick a random allotment of either gold or ore or banners (another unneccesary currency.) Why not just balance the resource gain properly instead of having a random resource dump at random intervals? Another complaint would be that in that original, almost every piece of equipment, and almost every block, was permanently upgradeable OUTSIDE of an actual game. Furthermore, they were NOT RNG, lootcrate-esque drops. You saved up for them and knew exactly what you were getting. Here, you still farm up resources, but then you throw in the slot machine and get a certain type of upgrade, say for troops, but it will be random what troop it buffs, what kind of buff it is, and the rarity of the buff. Given that the game costs money, there is no freemium mobile in-app purchase here, but this feels like a remnant of their block fortress empires mobile game with lootboxes. The RNG-based progression has no place in pc gaming and the game is worse for its inclusion here. On top of that, these buffs aren't each an incremental gain in power. No, instead you must choose only a handful at the start of any game to be active, and those are all you get. Remember how you could craft a slew of mods in the original for your favorite gun/turret to custom tailor it to your playstyle? Yep, thats prettymuch gone. So overall you do not feel like you're making tangible progress on your account overall, besides tech level unlocking new things. But every game you start you are effectively just as week as when you first started playing, aside from a couple RNG card buffs from lootboxes. Lastly, I'd comment that certain elements of the more RTS-style block fortress mobile game, block fortress war, are not carried over. Here, you can get troops, but from what I've seen they're incredibly weak. Your troops just automatically walk towards the nearest enemy, wherever they are or whatever enemy type they are. If your troops are ranged with guns, they easily get massacred by any enemy melee troops. And the enemy will VASTLY outnumber your troops. Instead of respawning waves of troops from your base like in BF war, here you get only one initial spawn, and that's it. Additionally, gone is the feature of custom-tailoring the equipment of your troops. Now, you only get to choose between the same generic upgrades for all troops, adding either a sergeant, medic, or scout to the squad. The whole design of how the player's troops have been implemented make them feel more like roadblocks designed to occupy the enemy for a few more seconds before you the player will still have to deal with them, rather than anything fun and powerful and worth building around. In the end this game just feels frustratingly unpolished. The fun of grinding to power up your favorite weapons and turrets is gone, replaced by RNG lootbox-esque buff drops. And the resource economy income is severely undertuned, making the game infuriatingly difficult. The RTS elements of BF War feel like a cheap gimmick here that isn't worth bothering with. I really hope the devs take time to perfect this game, and treat like a full PC game instead of a mobile game. Strip out the RNG, add actual incremental progression that is permanent, and playtest your game to ensure that it feels balanced and enjoyable. This isn't the mobile freemium market anymore, and a flashy coat of cool graphics won't make up for poor design decisions hidden underneath.

也是一代老玩家了，从1代到战争到帝国再到现在的2代，中间断断续续玩的起码也有10年了吧 2代从某种程度上说确实把前3部都缝合了一下，但是该怎么说呢，很多没缝到点上，就比如1代的mod系统，在这2代变成了类似Roguelike游戏的局内选择奖励，虽说有局外给的全球通用mod，但是开放的数量和星球等级绑定，最多也就5个，换到新星球就得从1开始（而且全球mod解锁还能出重复的，建议能给个排序以及快速回收功能）；再说回局内的奖励选项，它经常会给一些我用不到的奖励，比如给我一些我用不到的强化以及解锁我用不到的炮台，这就导致守旗帜的性价比变得有点低。但是我更建议在生存模式给个额外的局外成长，或者让全球mod不被星球等级限制，的毕竟每个星球的装备升级还有升级上限是单独的，到了新的星球会让人觉得之前的努力都付之东流，有点难受 话说能不能出个蓝图和配置物品栏功能，这样每次开局就不用手动再造基础的雏形了（虽然已经可以长按左键快速建造了）。 然后是小兵，我原本以为是能和战争一样自定义的，后来发现是我想多了（毕竟游戏也就那么大，都放一起确实不好做，也是希望战争也能出个2代，毕竟战争的游戏形式我还挺喜欢的），不过小兵确实厉害，但是不容易和炮塔配合，他跑的太远了 ，而且不能操控。 但是从总体上来说，确实比1代要好上不少，并且有自定义地图功能，从某种程度上也是缝上了帝国的进攻防守pvp（就是装备种类没有帝国那样花样多）就是现在刚发售，大佬们也还在慢慢建设，也是未来可期，不过还是建议加强下开局资源，优化新手教程，削弱部分boss（主要是不死之躯buff，复活cd太短了双生buss好歹能控血，在前期没有喷射背包等快速移动手段且生命值低的情况下不死之躯buff会让人很难受）以及能让新手尽快解锁自动聚光灯和自动探测器等科技，毕竟很多玩家也是第一次接触这个游戏，如果前期没有说明清楚，那只会这些新玩家难以体会到游戏的乐趣 26.1.6 这么久都没更新？没了？

游戏是好游戏，但希望能在二代里复刻block fortress war的战役模式，希望也能体验进攻的感觉。另外那个版本也是能体验其他种族的，还有英雄技能设定，不知道能不能在2代体验到。 本来是好评，官方是怎么把下面三个性能放在一起的。可以不断招小怪（所有boss自带功能），吸收死掉小怪的生命，每次最多受到1点伤害
Not a fan. Looks good but does a bad job teaching you how to play.

不愧是出了好几个小品级独立游戏，并多年吃游戏制作这碗饭的厂，制作水平相当稳定 了解到一些基本规则以后就可以爽玩了，阻止玩家爽起来的主要原因是——在开始游戏前或者重置地图后，可以按T来随机地形，选到一个好的地图就赢一半。地形方块都是可以破坏的，木头树叶土地，这些遮挡视野的东西全都破坏掉才能让炮台更好的发挥 目前仍有一些bug会影响游玩，不过这游戏才出来几天，已经可以玩爽了 游戏的内容感觉少了点什么，玩家亲自战斗、炮台、士兵、机器人、陷阱、一点点肉鸽元素看似挺多，但升级太单一了，敌人也是堆血堆伤，自己这边也就是堆血堆伤，没啥特色，希望后边可以搞点更有创意的东西 ———— 短短几天修复了大量bug，做出了非常多的调整，甚至某些玩法都经历了大量整改，一切都是为了玩家的“爽“，难度也从哪个各个角度大幅度下调，如果说一开始是从抵抗敌人”硬核“的进攻中获得成就感，那么现在就是少量削减成就感而大幅度增加爽感，你依然需要大量时间去肝来一步一步解锁新物品，但现在在解锁新物品的道路上没有那么严重的挫败感了 真是得夸奖一下制作组，预备下一款游戏的同时对这款已发布的游戏毫不懈怠，积极与玩家交流意见，热衷于改善游戏体验，同时有自己的制作思路，由于国内与国外不通网，所以国外通过discord可以直接联网而国内不行，制作组这次更新还专门做了中国的“局域网”，以便中国玩家使用社区功能，对玩家的态度可以说是非常好，不像某些国产拿着相当不错的题材与创意却一年都放不出一个好屁，还有某些自我感觉良好热衷于和玩家对喷的
他们公司的游戏真的是从小玩到现在，英雄城堡，虫虫大作战，方块堡垒真的都很好玩！看到就直接入了，毫不犹豫，他们的游戏游戏性绝对高！！！真的非常非常希望官方能出多人合作！！这真的很重要！！Co-op Mode Pls！！！！！！！！！！！

Tentative review so far because I do sort of enjoy it, but some bad design choices are really hampering the game. It feels like a mobile port of the original game without any of the things you'd expect in a PC native version. The upgrade system is pretty terrible. There are menus in menus and you have to do things like equip mods every level. Tons of currency types that aren't well explained and feel very mobile game. Loot boxes whenever you spent for upgrade mods, which are needed to play, so your run can be tanked by bad RNG. The absolute worst offender is the terrain and weapons. It's almost impossible to get a map in the starting world where you can actually use turrets properly as the terrain is way to chaotic and the guns will refuse to shoot at enemies right next to them that are taking them out. If the enemy can shoot the gun, from 10 feet away, the effing machine gun should be able to shoot the enemy. Also, the need to get all those various premium currencies mid battle mean placing your barracks in a good place even harder. And worst of all, the bloody trees are a menace.

The game was not supposed to be like this. I bought it only because Block Fortress 1 represents my childhood and was one of my favorite games. Well, I can't say the same for this one. Extremely unbalanced game, you don't earn enough to be able to repair your base from a previous attack. I struggle to get past the second level at round 20 (2 Bosses in one round) when it should be a fun game, focused more on defense and building. Instead you will recive a game where you have to work hard and get angry every time because of the lack of resources and bosses that are too difficult. The game is too similar to how it was on the phone in terms of the (too many) resources present and the progression mechanics. From watching a lot of videos and opinions about the game, I can only say that in its current state the gameplay stops at a simple "build some pillars with some snipers and lasers and finish the level". No. A game is not fun this way. I would like to build a fortified fort with different types of weapons for different types of mobs. Not 3 walls with 3 weapons on them and then a horde of a mix of mobs that are way too op for the resources you earn (not to mention the bosses). I saw that the developers are already releasing balance updates but even now it's really too unbalanced and not fun for how it "should be" (a game where you build an armed fort). For now, I'll leave a negative review until the game improves enough to be called fun and like when we played it as kids.

This generation can no longer customize weapons and building modules like the first generation, and this generation can no longer customize soldiers' weapons and equipment like in "war". Perhaps these changes were made to make the game simpler, but its playability has dropped significantly. [h3] Bad level design [/h3] I seriously suspect that the author has not played the levels designed by himself! For instance, the difficulty design of the seventh level, "Defense Battle", is definitely not "medium difficulty" but "almost impossible to complete"! The zombies' health recovery speed is terrifyingly fast, especially the third boss's health recovery speed is even as fast as that of the Hulk! However, humans have only a pitiful 400 gold coins and 150 metals! Although there was support later, it was only 300 gold coins and 200 metals! This level might only be cleared by using "bug" [h1] bug [/h1] Some modules that were not supposed to require an upgrade actually had an "upgrade" button displayed incorrectly. However, these "upgrade" buttons were ineffective and caused players to spend game currency but get no benefit at all. For example, the "laser cannon invisibility" upgrade button.

As a fan of the original mobile game I played when I was far younger seeing this pop up brought back some nostalgia. The game feels a bit too similar to the mobile game although the maps are far better in terms of looks etc. The game play feels different in a strange way, I understand what they were going for with the planet upgrade system but I think the universal upgrades from the first game were better. I think the main problem is scale, the maps are quite large but all but a few turrets have pathetic ranges, by the time they start shooting they will probably be killed in one or two shots by a ranged enemy and then you have to pay an expensive price to replace them (the economy is another thing that needs balancing). This means the ideal (and maybe only) strategy is build a giant tower with laser turrets which wins easily making every other turret feel pointless. I don't know what to suggest to improve the game except doubling resources and enemies and dramatically increasing all the turret ranges. The game basically punishes you for using any other strategy except big laser tower. I might come back to the game later but in it's current state it feels a bit early access, the menus are pretty bad too you open a menu to open a menu etc. If you command a bot to move it opens 3 (different) menus on top of eachother? which I assume is just a bug

Good initial start but quickly becomes tedious with clear meta builds outshining all other possible builds. just simply build a tall tower on you bunker and slap lasers and snipers on it, built it out like a giant mushroom, end game content. I wish there was more depth to the game, such as complex commands to your troops such as deployment options, patrol routes, guard this area, etc. they really missed out in this area, although there are simple follow me and retreat commands they kind of fall flat when you are playing. maybe voice lines from your bots like "help im being over run over here" would bring some life to this lifeless game. i also feel like a lot of the maps and resources are annoyingly sparse, it leads me to just build the meta build, no walls, just a big mushroom with turrets on it, cause i sure dont have the resources to repair walls, or build them in most games. maybe instead of resources it can cost a base block for every round you can build 50, some blocks cost more but essentially they are free from the typical resources you need for turrets and people. Game has a lot of potential but right now its basically a port from the 5 dollar mobile game you can get on your phone with not much extra added into the game. AI still has the basic walk straight towards closest base material as well, so cheesing the AI is pretty easy, it cant be that hard to code AI in 2025 i think chat gpt could write the code for this ai in a few seconds. Boring predictable AI, leads to boring rounds, and overall causing players to lose interest pretty fast. Summary: save your money until more content or updates arrive, this game is not worth 4 times the cost of its mobile counterpart.

EDIT: 3/12/25 Have to change my review to Negative after an extremely slow pace of updates, and dealing with the game's inability to properly align blocks like windows with the Wall or Floor tool for the 517th time. There are so many bugs, lack of QOL and features that makes building anything in this game so unbearable. I'm out. ---- Fun game, marred by some less-than-desirable problems. The good: - Gameplay loop of managing resources and building before defending waves of enemies is generally fun. Balance is a bit all over the place but that's a separate topic. - Soundtrack is okay, most of it straight up is from BF: War, though they did add some new ones. - Game looks and runs pretty well. The bad: - Enemy variation is very lacking. Goblocks are the only real race where you have a healthy selection of enemies to fight. Compare that to Zomblocks who have 6 total units, 2 of which could be heroes (Brute + Overlord) and 1 that is unused (now do the math). It doesn't really matter to what planet you go, you're going to be fighting Goblocks for the majority of the time. - Enemy-specific mechanics: some are very boring (Blockoid Warrior) or insanely powerful (Blockbot Nano). Arcanus I frankly don't understand why it's an enemy that exist, given Blockoids in BF: War had a lot of very cool mechanics (such as being able to wield and fire multiple weapons!) Heck, the Master Blaster can fire multiple projectiles. - Downtime: I don't know what to call this point but there are moments in the game where you're actively trying to survive and scrap by for every minerals. Then you cross a threshold and the game plateaus very hard in difficulty. I'd chalk it up to balance I guess. - Missing QOL: This is mainly pertaining to creative mode, but having to open a wheel for plane/line mode feels kinda backwards to me. Space Engineers had it almost perfect, with being able to easily select, place and delete large amounts of blocks, plane/line through mouse, symmetry mode, rotating assets etc. That all being said, it's still a fun game, but it does need a bit of love in some areas so it truly stands out. 7/10

Like others I want this game to be good, I played Block Fortress 1 all the time when I was younger, but this just misses the mark. Building is tedious and even with them removing the range bonus from your meta towers, theyre still meta towers when you just use high range turrets on them (such as lasers having true infinite range now.) The mineral system is decent, you get to pick a certain amount of mods depending on the wave count you're on, but your mods are not permanently in slots like the original game. The pace of updates is painfully slow though, the game hasn't gotten a single content update since I got it 4 months ago. The difference races both don't have much enemy variety and feel kind of samey (except the zomblocks), blockbots and blockoids both feel like goblocks with extra health and damage. There is a troop system, but half of them are super underpowered (just spam assassins with mods to increase squad size, nothing else compares), you also can't command them in any, so they will likely stand in front of an enemy and just die. Somehow this feels more like a mobile game than the original mobile only Block Fortress game, kinda sucks to see. (and on the mobile version, even if you've paid and linked a pc account, they still have the big shiny microtransaction shop every time you open the main menu)

I think it's fun. Its definitely slop to some extent, but so was the original game. I do find it interesting how they tried to implement more factions with different themes. In Block Fortress 1, there were only the goblocks, but now there are zomblocks and some other factions I haven't played far enough into a planet to see. Some people complain about the balancing of the game, and while it is kinda difficult, it's not impossible. Easily the best mod in the game HAS to be power pack, especially for miners. If you get the global mod power pack for miners, you're already starting the game with a strong mineral economy. If you're playing on normal, then this should be a cakewalk, since you can exchange minerals for gold. However, it is a GRINDFEST to get that. To put it in perspective; you get 3 planet minerals for each successful round you complete on a planet. You need 60 artic planet minerals for the ore miner power pack global mod. That means you have to survive 20 rounds to get a global mod. Now, granted it isn't that bad since there are boss rounds, and surviving a boss round grants you 10 "rainbow" minerals. Rainbow minerals can be exchanged for any type of mineral in the game. So, if you wanted to, you could dump all 10 rainbow minerals into artic and cut it down to about 16 rounds. That being said, the bosses are BUSTED, but again not unbeatable. The bosses can 1 shot level 2 walls. Since level 2 walls are your bread and butter (because who uses level 1 walls if they cost gold instead and have less health?), having the first boss 1 shot all level 2 walls is kinda a bad idea. Maybe 2 or 3 hits can take down a wall (lets not completely neuter the first boss here) and increase the health instead, or not. The first boss has a GIGANTIC health pool. I was able to beat him by just kiting him away from the base so he wouldn't completely destroy everything. Again, balancing is a bit rough but not awful. I'd argue for these singleplayer games, balancing doesn't matter that much but you still need to take it into consideration. I'd say the 2nd boss of survival rounds (if there are any more after the first) should one shot level 2 walls, since at that point you would've invested in level 3 or 4 walls instead. My one legitimate complaint I think most people will agree on: WHY IS THERE NO CO-OP? Y'all missed a HUGE opportunity here. Friendslop and co-op games like REPO and Lethal Company have short lived audiences, sure, BUT ITS STILL AN OPPORTUNITY! The first Block Fortress had Co-op, but this doesn't? Come on, add co-op. Immediately.

I genuinely like this game, but I'm leaving a negative review for now. Why? Controls and UI The bot controls are bugged. With the collector bot, pressing the menu button brings up two menus stacked on top of each other: the radial menu and another game UI. It's clunky and feels broken. Settings The settings are honestly abysmal. Missing features include: Auto-start Gameplay control options Pause when the game is in the background More granular settings in general Account Linking? Why is account linking required? This isn't a live service game. Unless it's needed for mobile cross-save, I don't see the point. If anything, you're just increasing your own operating costs. Not really my problem, but it's something I'd reconsider. Troops Feel Useless Troops don't really feel worth using. I'd love to see a barracks building that spawns units automatically, with unit limits based on the number of barracks you own. Give them meaningful damage and let them become an actual part of the strategy. My Biggest Complaint: After Action Reports The after-action reports are painful. It feels like 5 to 10 clicks just to get through them. No thanks. And don't even get me started on the balance. Adding loot boxes and twenty different resources doesn't improve the game. It actually subtracts from the experience. Complexity isn't depth. Global Mods I love the idea of global modifiers. I think that's one of the strongest concepts in the game. That said, it still needs refinement. Again, I really do love this game. That's why this review is frustrating to write. But in its current state, I can't recommend it in good conscience. Feature Requests Pistons and wires. I want automation. Asking for a friend. Mining. Infinite worlds. World generation settings. The ability to physically land your spaceship on a planet. Massive battles that lag my PC into dust. More logistics systems. Cars. Trains. Hell, make it moddable like Minecraft. Seriously. People would add half this stuff themselves. More than anything, I wish this game felt closer to the original, just brought to PC. Keep the new features, but make them unobtrusive instead of constantly putting themselves in front of the player experience. There's a fantastic game buried in here. I can see it. I just don't think it's there yet. but i will continue to play it as this game is near and dear to my heart and child hood.
